hero.title: A boilerplate built for modern Angular
hero.description: A ready-to-use application foundation with Signals, zoneless change detection, SSR, hydration, deferrable views, and reactive data APIs.

architecture.title: An application foundation to build on
architecture.description: The boilerplate collects the infrastructure common to modern Angular applications and leaves business logic to the project created from the fork. This page shows how the main architectural choices work.

signals.title: Signal-based state
signals.description: signal() manages local state, computed() derives values, and reactive primitives extend the same model to dependent and asynchronous data.

defer.title: Deferrable views
defer.description: @defer delays non-essential dependencies and moves work out of the application's initial loading path.

hydration.title: SSR and hydration
hydration.description: Angular can generate HTML on the server and reuse it during browser hydration instead of rebuilding the page from scratch.

resources.title: Resource APIs
resources.description: resource() and httpResource() connect asynchronous data to the Signals model with explicit value, loading, and error states.

forms.title: Signal Forms
forms.description: Signal Forms provide a Signals-based model for building typed forms and managing field state and validation.

service.title: Modern dependency injection
service.description: @Service() provides a compact syntax for root-provided services, while @Injectable remains available for more specific configurations.

signals.title: Signals make state explicit
signals.description: signal() holds mutable state and computed() derives other values from it. Angular updates the parts of the UI that depend on these Signals when their value changes.
signals.computed: This value derives from the signal above and updates when that signal changes.

rendering.title: Render on the server, hydrate when needed
rendering.description: SSR, hydration, and incremental hydration let you choose when work moves from the server to the browser. With @defer, you can also keep non-essential code out of the initial load.
rendering.ssrDescription: The server generates meaningful HTML before the browser runs the application. This improves the initial render and provides readable content before hydration completes.
rendering.hydrationDescription: Angular reuses the DOM produced by the server and connects the application behavior in the browser. Event Replay preserves interactions that happen before hydration finishes.
rendering.deferDescription: With incremental hydration, @defer blocks can be rendered on the server and hydrated later. Triggers such as viewport, interaction, and idle determine when a section becomes interactive.
rendering.error: The deferred section could not be loaded.
rendering.deferredDescription: This section loads through Angular's deferrable-view system. With incremental hydration, the server can produce the content while the browser waits to hydrate it until the configured trigger fires.
rendering.deferredNote: The component keeps its Signals-based state throughout hydration.

data.title: Async data becomes reactive state
data.description: Resource APIs connect asynchronous operations to Signals. They are useful when the result of a request should participate directly in the UI state.
data.resource: resource() represents a Signals-driven asynchronous operation and exposes its value, status, loading, and error state.
data.httpResource: httpResource() connects HttpClient with the Resource API model. Requests continue to use the application's HTTP infrastructure and interceptors.
data.linkedSignal: linkedSignal() creates writable state connected to another state. It is useful when a user choice should follow a source that can change.

forms.title: Forms built on Signals
forms.description: Signal Forms introduce a reactive form model for new applications. A Signal-based model can become a typed field tree with declarative validation rules.
forms.note: Reactive Forms remain available and are a solid choice for existing applications. You can adopt Signal Forms gradually when the project is ready.

di.title: Modern dependency injection
di.description: @Service() is the compact syntax for a root-provided service. For the common case, it removes the explicit @Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' }) configuration and works naturally with inject() for dependencies.
di.note: Use @Injectable when you need constructor injection, a non-root scope, or advanced provider configuration.
